stories.headline: Samsung Orders ~20 EUV Machines From ASML in 10+ Trillion Won Deal for P5 Fab

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics ordered approximately 20 EUV lithography machines from ASML worth over 10 trillion won ($7.4 billion) for its Pyeongtaek P5 fab.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics ordered approximately 20 EUV lithography machines from ASML worth over 10 trillion won for its Pyeongtaek P5 fab

key_facts.fact: Including DUV tools from ASML and Canon, the total lithography equipment order reaches roughly 70 units for the P5 facility.
key_facts.excerpt: Including deep ultraviolet (DUV) tools, the total lithography equipment order reaches roughly 70 units

key_facts.fact: The machines will boost production of sixth-generation 1c DRAM and HBM4 memory chips, with Samsung supplying chips to Nvidia for the Rubin GPU platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Boost production of sixth-generation 1c DRAM and HBM4 memory chips... Samsung supplies chips to Nvidia for the Rubin GPU platform

key_facts.fact: Samsung currently operates about 40 EUV machines, roughly twice SK hynix's fleet. SK hynix recently signed its own 12 trillion won ASML deal for ~20 EUV machines.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung currently operates about 40 EUV machines — approximately twice SK hynix's fleet. SK hynix recently signed its own 12 trillion won ASML deal for roughly 20 EUV machines

key_facts.fact: P5 Phase 1 cleanroom completion is expected in Q1 2027, with equipment delivery and installation beginning in Q2 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Phase 1 cleanroom completion expected Q1 2027, equipment delivery begins Q2 2027

sources.title: Samsung Orders ~20 EUV Machines for P5 Fab in Over 10 Trillion Won Deal

stories.headline: Spain's Xoople Raises $130M Series B to Build AI Earth-Observation Satellite Constellation

key_facts.fact: Xoople raised a $130 million Series B, bringing its total funding to $225 million, to develop a satellite constellation that collects earth data for training AI models.
key_facts.excerpt: Xoople, which is developing a satellite constellation to collect earth data for training AI models, raised a $130M Series B, bringing its total funding to $225M

key_facts.fact: The round was led by Nazca Capital, with participation from MCH Private Equity, CDTI (a Spanish government tech fund), Buenavista Equity Partners, and Endeavor Catalyst.
key_facts.excerpt: Series B led by Nazca Capital. Other investors include MCH Private Equity, CDTI, a tech development fund backed by the Spanish government, Buenavista Equity Partners, and Endeavor Catalyst

key_facts.fact: Xoople signed a deal with US defense contractor L3Harris Technologies to begin building sensors for its spacecraft, designed to collect data 'two orders of magnitude better than existing monitoring systems.'
key_facts.excerpt: Deal with U.S. space and defense contractor L3Harris Technologies to begin building sensors for Xoople's spacecraft, designed to collect a stream of data that is going to be two orders of magnitude better than existing monitoring systems

key_facts.fact: The company's valuation is reported to be 'in unicorn territory' after the current fundraising round.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's valuation is in unicorn territory after the current fundraising round

stories.headline: Japan Accelerates Physical AI Deployment as Labor Shortage Projected to Hit 11 Million by 2040

key_facts.fact: Japan's METI announced it aims to capture 30% of the global physical AI market by 2040, with a budget of ¥387.3 billion for AI foundation models, data infrastructure, and physical AI within a broader ¥1.23 trillion AI and semiconductor package.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan aims to capture 30% of the global physical AI market by 2040. Budget: ¥387.3 billion specifically for domestic AI foundation models, data infrastructure, and physical AI. Broader AI Package: ¥1.23 trillion for AI and semiconductor development in fiscal year 2026

key_facts.fact: Japan has 450,500 industrial robots operating in its factories, and Japanese manufacturers control approximately 70% of the global industrial robotics market, including five of the world's ten largest firms (FANUC, Yaskawa, Kawasaki, Nachi-Fujikoshi).
key_facts.excerpt: 450,500 industrial robots operating in Japanese factories. Japanese manufacturers control ~70% of global industrial robotics market. Five of world's ten largest are Japanese (FANUC, Yaskawa, Kawasaki, Nachi-Fujikoshi)

key_facts.fact: Mujin has deployed AI-powered robotic arms across more than 100 warehouse sites, with throughput equivalent to three to four human workers per station.
key_facts.excerpt: Mujin deployed AI-powered robotic arms across 100+ warehouse sites, automating palletizing tasks with throughput equivalent to three to four human workers per station

key_facts.fact: Shimizu Corporation's Robo-Welder has demonstrated a roughly 70% reduction in required human welding hours on active construction sites.
key_facts.excerpt: Shimizu's Robo-Welder system demonstrating a roughly 70% reduction in required human welding hours

key_facts.fact: Japan projects a shortage of 11 million workers by 2040 and 570,000 care workers, with nursing positions drawing only 1 applicant per 4.25 openings.
key_facts.excerpt: Worker Shortage Projection: 11 million workers by 2040. Care Worker Gap: 570,000 shortage projected by 2040. Only 1 applicant per 4.25 openings in nursing

key_facts.fact: Japan's physical AI market was valued at approximately $307 million in 2025 and is projected to reach $6.76 billion by 2035.
key_facts.excerpt: Japan's physical AI market worth approximately $307 million in 2025, projected to reach $6.76 billion by 2035

sources.title: In Japan, the robot isn’t coming for your job; it’s filling the one nobody wants
Japan is deploying robots not to replace workers but because there’s no one left to hire

stories.headline: China Tightens Drone Rules With Mandatory Registration and Real-Time Tracking by May 1

key_facts.fact: Two national drone standards take effect May 1, 2026, requiring real-name registration for all civil drones and mandating that unactivated or deactivated drones be technically incapable of flight.
key_facts.excerpt: May 1, 2026: Two national standards take effect. Real-name registration mandatory for all civil drones. Unactivated or deactivated drones must be technically incapable of flight

key_facts.fact: Drones weighing 250 grams or more require mandatory safety management and real-time location reporting, with micro drones capped at 50 meters altitude and light drones (under 4kg) at 120 meters.
key_facts.excerpt: Drones 250+ grams require mandatory safety management and real-time location reporting. Micro drones: capped at 50 meters. Light drones (under 4kg): limited to 120 meters above ground level

key_facts.fact: Professional drone pilots reported a 'cliff-like drop in demand' after the regulations were finalized, with some pilots facing fines or confiscation for incomplete registration.
key_facts.excerpt: Professional pilot 'Nike' reported a 'cliff-like drop in demand' after rules finalized. Some pilots faced fines or confiscation for incomplete registration

key_facts.fact: By end of 2024, China had approximately 273,000 licensed drone pilots versus 2.17 million registered drones, indicating most consumer drones were operated by unlicensed users.
key_facts.excerpt: By end of 2024: approximately 273,000 licensed pilots versus 2.17 million registered drones — indicating most consumer drones operated by unlicensed users

key_facts.fact: Smaller drone manufacturers face cost barriers from new remote identification and registration lock requirements, while larger firms like DJI are better positioned to adapt.
key_facts.excerpt: Smaller manufacturers face cost barriers from new remote identification and registration lock requirements, while larger firms like DJI — emphasizing compliance — are better positioned to adapt

sources.title: China tightens drone regulations amid growing industry
China’s tighter drone rules usher in industry adjustment period

stories.headline: California's Largest Proposed Data Center Faces Opposition in Imperial County

key_facts.fact: A developer plans a nearly 1 million square foot, 330MW data center on 75 acres near Aten Road and Clark Road in Imperial County, adjacent to residential neighborhoods and less than a mile from schools.
key_facts.excerpt: Nearly 1 million square feet... 330 megawatts... 75 acres near Aten Road and Clark Road outside Imperial, California; adjacent to two residential neighborhoods with hundreds of homes and less than a mile from schools and playgrounds

key_facts.fact: Imperial city officials filed a 231-page court complaint citing concerns about noise, hazardous emissions, fires, explosions, and toxins, saying they were not adequately consulted and environmental review was insufficient.
key_facts.excerpt: Imperial city officials filed a 231-page court complaint citing concerns about noise, hazardous emissions, fires, explosions, and toxins... were not adequately consulted and that environmental review was insufficient

key_facts.fact: Residents are gathering signatures for a November 2026 ballot initiative called the 'Imperial County Data Center Prohibition Act' that would block all data centers in the county.
key_facts.excerpt: Residents are gathering signatures for a potential November 2026 ballot initiative called the 'Imperial County Data Center Prohibition Act' to block all data centers in the county

key_facts.fact: The developer's claims that the facility would rely on renewable energy and recycled water have been disputed, and California's Little Hoover Commission noted it is 'unclear whether such commitments would be legally binding.'
key_facts.excerpt: Developer claims facility would rely on renewable energy and recycled water... California's Little Hoover Commission noted these 'claims have been disputed, and it is unclear whether such commitments would be legally binding'

key_facts.fact: The Imperial County Board of Supervisors is scheduled to discuss the critical lot merger vote on April 7, which would determine whether construction can proceed.
key_facts.excerpt: Imperial County Board of Supervisors scheduled to discuss the lot merger at 11 a.m. Tuesday, April 7

sources.title: California’s largest data center plan rouses Imperial County
Imperial County supervisors to hold key vote on controversial data center project

stories.headline: SpaceX Scrubs Starlink Launch Seconds Before Ignition at Vandenberg Due to Winds

key_facts.fact: SpaceX halted the Starlink 17-35 launch seconds before ignition at Vandenberg Space Force Base on April 6 due to upper-level winds.
key_facts.excerpt: Controllers scrubbed seconds before ignition due to upper level winds

key_facts.fact: The mission was carrying 25 Starlink V2 Mini satellites destined for low Earth orbit, with a rescheduled launch window of 4:03-8:03 PM PT on April 6.
key_facts.excerpt: Payload: 25 Starlink satellites. Rescheduled attempt targets 4:03 to 8:03 p.m. PT on April 6, 2026

key_facts.fact: The Falcon 9 booster assigned to the mission was making its first flight, with a planned autonomous landing on the drone ship 'Of Course I Still Love You' in the Pacific Ocean.
key_facts.excerpt: First flight for this particular Falcon 9 booster. Following stage separation, the first-stage booster will attempt an autonomous drone ship landing on 'Of Course I Still Love You' in the Pacific Ocean

sources.title: Falcon 9 Today, April 6: SpaceX Scrubs Vandenberg Starlink Launch
Falcon 9 launch of Starlink satellites from Vandenberg SFB scheduled for Sunday

stories.headline: Artemis II Completes Trajectory Correction on Flight Day 5, Crew Set for Monday Flyby

key_facts.fact: The Artemis II crew completed an outbound correction burn at 11:03 PM EDT on April 5, lasting 17.5 seconds, to refine Orion's trajectory toward the Moon.
key_facts.excerpt: The outbound correction burn occurred at 11:03 p.m. EDT and lasted 17.5 seconds, refining Orion's trajectory toward the Moon

key_facts.fact: The crew tested the Orion Crew Survival System (OCSS) suit, performing pressurization checks, leak tests, seat entry simulations, and mobility assessments in preparation for the flyby.
key_facts.excerpt: Crew completed critical testing of the Orion Crew Survival System (OCSS) suit, including pressurization checks, leak tests, and mobility assessments

key_facts.fact: Orion's closest lunar approach will be at 7:02 PM EDT April 6 at 4,070 miles above the surface, with maximum distance from Earth of 252,760 miles at 7:07 PM — surpassing Apollo 13's 1970 record of 248,655 miles.
key_facts.excerpt: 7:02 p.m.: Closest approach at 4,070 miles above lunar surface. 7:07 p.m.: Maximum distance from Earth at 252,760 miles. Artemis II will surpass Apollo 13's 1970 record of 248,655 miles

key_facts.fact: The crew will experience approximately 40 minutes of communications blackout as Orion passes behind the far side of the Moon starting at 6:44 PM EDT, with 'Earthrise' and signal reacquisition at 7:25 PM.
key_facts.excerpt: 6:44 p.m.: Communication blackout as Orion passes behind the Moon (approximately 40 minutes). 7:25 p.m.: Earthrise and communications reacquired

key_facts.fact: The crew reviewed 30 final lunar surface targets for observation and photography during the flyby, which is scheduled for 2:45-9:40 PM EDT on April 6.
key_facts.excerpt: Reviewed final 30 lunar surface targets for observation and photography

sources.title: Artemis II Flight Day 5: Correction Burn Complete
Artemis II Flight Day 5: Crew Demos Suits, Readies for Lunar Flyby
